title: Most news feeds are broken because they treat everyone the same.
body:
We have spent the last few decades building algorithms that optimize for engagement. The goal was simple. Keep people clicking. Keep them on the page. But that approach usually ignores what you actually care about. It gives you more of what you already saw rather than what you need to know.

The next phase of personalized news is not about serving more content. It is about serving the right context. We are moving toward a model where AI acts as a filter for noise, not a megaphone for volume. It should function like a smart assistant that understands your interests and respects your time.

At Headlinne, our roadmap is focused on this shift. We want to build tools that help you cut through the clutter and find the stories that actually matter to your day. This means prioritizing accuracy and nuance over outrage. It means giving you control over your feed instead of letting an algorithm decide for you.

Personalization should make you smarter, not just more addicted to your screen.
cta: You can see how we are building this at HEADLINNE.com.
